mind_map.central_node: Neem Baba: Traditional Ecological Knowledge, Ayurvedic Medicine, and Botanical Sustainability
plot_summary_nodes: Exposition > Resting Under the Neem Tree: Amber rests under a courtyard neem tree after school and feels as if the rustling leaves are speaking to her.
Inciting Incident > Meeting Neem Baba: Amber greets the tree politely ('Namaste!'), and the tree affectionately introduces itself as 'Neem Baba'.
Rising Action (Part I) > Botanical Origins & History: Neem Baba shares his Persian/Sanskrit heritage ('Azad Darakhte Hindi' / 'Azadirachta indica') and global presence.
Rising Action (Part II) > Environmental Role: Explains how neem trees purify air, trap dust, release oxygen, and provide shade for animals and humans.
Rising Action (Part III) > Medicinal Applications: Details how every part—leaves, bark, twigs (datun), and seeds—cures skin diseases, cleans teeth, and heals wounds.
Rising Action (Part IV) > Organic Agriculture: Explains how neem oil and seed cake act as eco-friendly pesticides and soil fertilizers without chemical pollution.
Resolution > Gratitude & Environmental Blessing: Amber thanks Neem Baba for his wisdom; Neem Baba blesses her, fostering environmental consciousness.
character_arc_nodes: Amber (Student): Curious, respectful young girl eager to learn traditional ecological wisdom.
Neem Baba (Personified Tree): Wise, benevolent, and ancient botanical mentor acting as a 'village pharmacy'.
theme_and_moral_nodes: Primary Theme > Ecological Sustainability & Indigenous Wisdom: Nature provides natural, non-toxic solutions for human health and agriculture.
Secondary Theme > Environmental Stewardship: Respecting, protecting, and planting trees for clean air and biodiversity.
Cross-Disciplinary Link > Ayurveda & Organic Farming: Traditional Indian medicine and chemical-free agricultural pest management.
Moral Lesson > Selfless Nature: Trees give shade, medicine, and clean air unconditionally.
key_grammar_nodes: Grammar Rule > Compound Words: Closed (courtyard, doorstep), Open (neem tree, air purification), and Hyphenated (cost-effective, eco-friendly).
Grammar Rule > Personification in Prose: Giving human voice, emotions, and memory to non-human botanical entities.
Vocabulary > Azadirachta indica (botanical name), Datun (chewed neem twig for dental care), Pesticide (pest killer), Purify (cleanse).
Expository Dialogue Format: Structured Q&A narrative conveying factual scientific and cultural information.
